_meta.purpose: Beef primal regions and the retail cuts under them. Nine regions to match the product's diagram convention; FSIS parents are recorded on each. Scores are 1 to 5 editorial judgments anchored to FSIS's tenderness statement (chuck and round less tender, loin and rib tender) and are labelled editorial.
_meta.scores_basis: tenderness_score 5 = most tender (tenderloin). richness_score 5 = fattiest / most marbled. Editorial, not measured.

regions.name: Chuck
regions.short_description: The shoulder. Hard-working, richly flavoured, full of connective tissue that rewards low and slow.
regions.long_description: USDA FSIS names chuck as one of the four major beef primals and notes it is less tender and generally needs moist heat. In barbecue that translates to smoking and braising: chuck roast cooked like a small brisket, and chuck short ribs that the Beef Board describes as flavourful, moist and tender when slow-cooked. The flat iron, cut from the top blade, is the exception: the Beef Board calls it the second most tender beef cut and it grills like a steak.
best_methods: grill (flat iron and Denver steak only)

retail_cuts.name: Chuck roast
retail_cuts.note: Often called the poor man's brisket. Wrap around 165 F, pull probe tender.

retail_cuts.name: Chuck short ribs
retail_cuts.note: Beef Board: tender when slow-cooked.

retail_cuts.name: Flat iron steak
retail_cuts.note: From the top blade. Second most tender beef cut (Beef Board). Slice across the grain.

retail_cuts.name: Denver steak
retail_cuts.note: From the centre of the under blade; high heat (Beef Board).

retail_cuts.name: Ground chuck
retail_cuts.note: 160 F, no exceptions.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Chuck roast roughly 1.5 hours per pound at 250 F. Approximate.
regions.rest_guidance: 30 to 60 minutes for a smoked roast; 5 minutes for a flat iron.
regions.slice_direction: Across the grain. Pull rather than slice when cooked to the tenderness window.
common_mistakes: Pulling a chuck roast at 165 F because the safety minimum is met; it is safe but tough.
Grilling chuck roast like a steak.
Slicing flat iron with the grain.

regions.name: Rib
regions.short_description: The middle of the back. Well marbled, tender, home of the ribeye and the prime rib roast.
regions.long_description: FSIS names rib as a major primal that can be cooked by dry heat. The ribeye steak and the standing rib roast come from here, as do beef back ribs. This is grilling and roasting territory; smoke is used for flavour on a rib roast, not to render collagen.

retail_cuts.name: Ribeye steak
retail_cuts.note: Well-marbled. The reverse sear (smoke low, then sear) suits thick ribeyes.

retail_cuts.name: Rib roast (prime rib)
retail_cuts.note: Beef Board: roasts rise 5 to 15 F after leaving the heat; stand 15 to 20 minutes.

retail_cuts.name: Beef back ribs
retail_cuts.note: Less meat than plate short ribs; smoke until the meat pulls back from the bone.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Rib roast: FSIS planning table 23 to 25 minutes per pound at 325 F, bone in. Reverse-seared ribeye: 45 to 60 minutes in smoke at 225 F then a hard sear. Approximate.
regions.rest_guidance: Steaks 5 to 10 minutes. Roasts 15 to 20 minutes (Beef Board).
common_mistakes: Cooking a ribeye to a tenderness window; it is not a collagen cut.
Skipping the rest on a rib roast, then losing the juice on the board.

regions.name: Short loin
regions.short_description: The front of the loin. Strip steak, T-bone, porterhouse and the tenderloin's thick end. Tender, leaner than rib.
regions.long_description: Part of the FSIS loin primal, which cooks by dry heat. FSIS itself notes the naming chaos here: the boneless top loin steak is sold as strip steak, Kansas City steak, N.Y. strip, hotel cut, ambassador steak and club sirloin steak. The tenderloin runs under the short loin and sirloin and is the most tender cut on the animal.

retail_cuts.name: Strip steak (New York strip)
retail_cuts.note: Also Kansas City, hotel cut, club sirloin (FSIS).

retail_cuts.name: T-bone and porterhouse
retail_cuts.note: Strip on one side of the bone, tenderloin on the other; the tenderloin side cooks faster.

retail_cuts.name: Tenderloin (filet mignon)
retail_cuts.note: Most tender, least fat. FSIS planning: whole tenderloin 45 to 60 minutes at 425 F.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Steaks 3/4 inch: FSIS planning 4 to 5 minutes per side on a grill. Approximate; the thermometer decides.
common_mistakes: Treating short loin as a low-and-slow cut.
Overcooking tenderloin, which has no fat to forgive it.

regions.name: Sirloin
regions.short_description: The back of the loin. Leaner steaks with big beef flavour, and the tri-tip.
regions.long_description: The rear sub-primal of the FSIS loin. Top sirloin steaks grill well; the tri-tip roast, which the Beef Board describes as boneless, fairly tender and full-flavoured, is the Santa Maria barbecue cut: roast or grill, then slice across a grain that changes direction partway along the roast.

retail_cuts.name: Top sirloin steak
retail_cuts.note: Lean; do not push past medium.

retail_cuts.name: Tri-tip roast
retail_cuts.note: Beef Board: roast or grill then slice across the grain. The grain changes direction at the bend.

retail_cuts.name: Sirloin bavette / flap
retail_cuts.note: Beef Board: hearty texture, marinate and grill; fajita meat.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Tri-tip: 60 to 90 minutes at 225 F then a sear. Approximate.
regions.slice_direction: Across the grain; on tri-tip, find the two grain directions and cut each half separately.
best_woods: oak (Santa Maria tradition is red oak)
common_mistakes: Slicing tri-tip in one direction end to end.
Cooking tri-tip to a collagen window; it is a steak-style cut.

regions.name: Brisket
regions.fsis_parent: chuck (retail convention treats brisket as its own primal)
regions.short_description: The breast. The Beef Board calls it tougher because it is used for movement, and ideal for low and slow. The centre of Central Texas barbecue.
regions.long_description: A whole packer brisket is two muscles: the flat (Beef Board: the leaner 'first cut', can be sliced or shredded) and the point (the less lean, juicier half). FSIS's own planning table has it braising at 325 F for a few hours; barbecue instead smokes it for most of a day at 225 to 250 F until the flat is probe tender. Safety is met at 145 F with a 3 minute rest; tenderness arrives some 50 degrees later.

retail_cuts.name: Whole packer brisket
retail_cuts.note: Flat plus point, 10 to 16 lb untrimmed.

retail_cuts.name: Brisket flat (first cut)
retail_cuts.note: Beef Board: the leaner half; sliced or shredded. Dries faster than the point.

retail_cuts.name: Brisket point
retail_cuts.note: Beef Board: the less lean, juicy half. Source of burnt ends.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Roughly 1 to 1.5 hours per pound at 225 to 250 F; 10 to 16 hours for a packer. Approximate. Start earlier than you think.
regions.rest_guidance: 1 to 2 hours wrapped, held above 140 F.
regions.slice_direction: Slice the flat and the point across their own grain; the two muscles run in different directions. Pencil-thick slices on the flat.
best_woods: oak (post oak is the Central Texas standard)
common_mistakes: Cooking to a number instead of probe feel.
Slicing the whole packer in one direction.
Skipping or shortening the rest.
Letting a long hold drop below 140 F.

regions.name: Plate
regions.fsis_parent: plate (Beef Board primal; below the rib)
regions.short_description: The belly behind the brisket. Plate short ribs, skirt steak and hanger. Rich, fatty, and two very different cooking personalities.
regions.long_description: Plate short ribs (dino ribs) are collagen cuts smoked to probe tender like brisket. Skirt steak is a thin, coarse-grained steak that wants very high heat for a very short time and a thin slice across the grain.

retail_cuts.name: Plate short ribs
retail_cuts.note: Probe tender between the bones; the meat pulls back a finger's width from the bone ends.

retail_cuts.name: Skirt steak
retail_cuts.note: Beef Board (inside skirt): robust flavour, marinate and grill hot for fajitas. Slice thin across the grain.

retail_cuts.name: Hanger steak
retail_cuts.note: One per animal. Remove the centre membrane.

regions.planning_time_guidance: Short ribs 6 to 8 hours at 250 to 275 F. Skirt 2 to 3 minutes a side over the hottest fire you have. Approximate.
regions.slice_direction: Skirt: thin, across the grain, at an angle. Short ribs: served on the bone or sliced across.
common_mistakes: Cooking skirt past medium; it turns to rope.
Slicing skirt with the grain.

regions.name: Flank
regions.fsis_parent: flank (Beef Board primal; below the loin)
regions.short_description: Lean, boneless, intensely beefy. The Beef Board's words: best marinated and grilled, or sliced thin.
regions.long_description: A single flat muscle with a pronounced grain. It has almost no fat, so it is cooked fast and hot to no more than medium, rested, and sliced thin across the grain. It is not a smoking cut.

retail_cuts.name: Flank steak
retail_cuts.note: Beef Board: lean and boneless, intense beef flavour, marinate and grill or slice thin for stir-fry.

regions.planning_time_guidance: 4 to 6 minutes per side over high heat. Approximate.
regions.slice_direction: Thin, across the grain, on a bias. This matters more on flank than on any other beef cut.
common_mistakes: Slicing with the grain.
Cooking past medium.

regions.name: Round
regions.short_description: The hind leg. Lean and, in FSIS's words, less tender. Roasts and steaks that want moist heat or a thin slice.
regions.long_description: FSIS names round as a major primal that, like chuck, is less tender and generally needs moist heat. Top round and eye of round make roast beef and jerky; bottom round braises. In barbecue the round is a smoked-roast-beef cut sliced paper thin, or a braise. It is not brisket and does not become brisket with time; it has too little fat.
best_methods: smoke to medium-rare then slice thin

retail_cuts.name: Top round roast
retail_cuts.note: FSIS planning: round or rump roast 30 to 35 minutes per pound at 325 F. Slice thin.

retail_cuts.name: Eye of round
retail_cuts.note: Jerky and deli-style roast beef.

retail_cuts.name: Bottom round / rump
retail_cuts.note: Pot roast.

regions.planning_time_guidance: FSIS planning: 30 to 35 minutes per pound at 325 F for a round roast. Approximate.
regions.rest_guidance: 15 to 20 minutes for a roast (Beef Board).
common_mistakes: Smoking a round roast to 200 F expecting pulled beef; it dries out.
Thick slices.

regions.name: Shank
regions.short_description: The leg below the knee. Tough, gelatinous, full of flavour. Braise it or smoke it into a shredded 'Thor's hammer'.
regions.long_description: Cross-cut shanks are the osso buco cut. FSIS's planning table simmers stew or cross-cuts covered in liquid for 2 to 3 hours. Whole smoked shank is a showpiece cook that follows shoulder logic: smoke, then braise or wrap until the meat falls from the bone.

retail_cuts.name: Cross-cut shank (osso buco)
retail_cuts.note: FSIS planning: cover with liquid, simmer 2 to 3 hours.

retail_cuts.name: Whole shank
retail_cuts.note: Smoke 3 hours, then braise covered until fork tender.

regions.planning_time_guidance: 2 to 3 hours simmering (FSIS planning); 6 to 8 hours smoke-then-braise. Approximate.
regions.slice_direction: Usually served on the bone or pulled.
common_mistakes: Dry heat only; without liquid or a wrap the shank never softens.
